advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the stale-entry guard to check the test function name in each --deselect node id (e.g. parse the module with ast and confirm the function exists), or narrow the docstring's claim to module-level coverage.
evidence: tests/unit/test_windows_sweep_deselect.py:23: _LINE = re.compile(r"^--(deselect|ignore)=(tests/[^:\s]+\.py)(::.+)?$") -- the node-id suffix is captured but never checked

Many entries are parametrized ids such as test_gate_step_tree_skew.py::test_absent_script_does_not_fail_the_build[_build-and-test.yml::lint::Complexity-baseline lock]. Renaming a workflow step changes that id and leaves the old line matching nothing, with no warning.
advisory.finding: test_every_listed_module_still_exists only checks that the module path in each --deselect line exists. It never checks the ::function or [param-id] part. Pytest's --deselect says nothing when a node id matches no test, so lines for deleted or renamed tests, or changed parametrize ids, stay in the lists without anyone noticing. The module docstring says the opposite: that no dead entry can be left behind.
scenarios: A test function listed in max-path.args is deleted or merged into another test. Its --deselect line now does nothing but stays in the list, so the class's fix-up bug overcounts the remaining work.

A workflow step is renamed, which changes the parametrize ids of test_gate_step_tree_skew. The old ids stay listed and do nothing. The renamed tests run on Windows and turn the sweep red, which looks like a new regression even though the failure was already known.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_every_listed_module_still_exists, for --deselect lines, take the function name after '::' (cut at '[') and check with ast.parse that the module defines it as a top-level FunctionDef or AsyncFunctionDef, or as a method of a class when the id has a Class:: segment. Or reword the docstring so it only promises module-level coverage.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend test_every_listed_module_still_exists to check that the test function in each `--deselect` node id is still defined in its module, not just that the module file exists.
evidence: tests/unit/test_windows_sweep_deselect.py:82: `if (match := _LINE.match(line)) and not (_ROOT / match.group(2)).is_file()` checks only group 2, the module path; group 3 (`::<test>[<param>]`) is never checked

tests/unit/test_windows_sweep_deselect.py:7-8 docstring: "every line still names a test module that exists, so a renamed or deleted module cannot leave a dead entry behind". Only a module rename is covered, not a test rename.

Named violating input: rename `test_cache_invalidated_on_file_deletion` in tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_cache.py. The line `--deselect=tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_cache.py::test_cache_invalidated_on_file_deletion` (file-locks.args, added by this diff) stays, the module still exists, and all four tests pass.
advisory.finding: test_every_listed_module_still_exists checks only that the module file named in each `--deselect` line exists, not that the test function inside it still exists. A renamed or deleted test leaves a stale deselect entry that the Linux gate never flags, and pytest silently skips a deselect id that matches nothing.
scenarios: A refactor renames a deselected test or changes its parametrize ids. The list then holds a dead entry, the renamed test fails on Windows again, and nothing on the Linux gate points to the leftover line.
A fix PR deletes a Windows-failing test but forgets its deselect line, so the defect-class bug looks open after the work is done.
advisory.suggested_fix: For each `--deselect` line with a `::` part, take the test name before any `[` and check that the module defines it. One way: `ast.parse` the module and look for a matching top-level `def`/`async def` or a `Class::method` pair. For a stronger check, run `pytest --collect-only -q <module>` and assert that the node id appears in the output.

advisory.finding: test_no_test_is_listed_in_two_classes compares exact lines only. It cannot see an overlap where one class has `--ignore=<module>` and another class has `--deselect=<module>::<test>` for the same module, so that test sits in two defect classes undetected.
scenarios: A future triage adds a deselect line for a module another class already ignores, so the two classes overlap without notice.
advisory.suggested_fix: Collect the `--ignore` module paths with the file each comes from. Then, for every `--deselect` line, assert that its group(2) module is not ignored by a different argfile.
